references.text: Jesus' answer to the question of whether he is greater than Abraham confirms his divine identity with the statement 'Before Abraham was, I am', which directly addresses the claim of being greater than the patriarch.
Here the Jews call Jesus equal with God, reflecting their reaction in John 8:53 where they ask if he makes himself greater than their father Abraham.
The Jews explain that they want to stone Jesus because, as a man, he makes himself God, a theme central to the discussion of his status in relation to Abraham.
Jesus explains that whoever has seen him has seen the Father, which supports his claim of being greater than Abraham by showing his unity with God.
Jesus asks to be restored to the glory he had with the Father before the world existed, confirming his existence before Abraham and his superior status.
Jesus claims that Abraham rejoiced to see his day, placing Abraham below Jesus in time and authority, and preparing the question of whether Jesus is greater than him.
